from keystone import config
from keystone.models import capital
from keystone.models.sustainability import Design, Family
base = dict(config.COST_ASSUMPTIONS)
print("hard$/sf  disc   gap/home   total(100)")
for hc in (325, 375, 425):
    for disc in (0.04, 0.05, 0.06):
        config.COST_ASSUMPTIONS["hard_cost_per_sqft"] = hc
        p = capital.plan(100, Family(), Design(), note_discount_rate=disc)
        print(f"{hc:>8} {disc:>5.0%} {p['per_unit_gap_after_public_sources']:>10,} {p['philanthropy_needed_total']:>12,}")
config.COST_ASSUMPTIONS.update(base)

Method: U-Net on NAIP 2022 RGB+NIR, OSM-labelled; developable = 50% of parking + 50% of lawn; 16 du/ac townhomes. Source: SB 4 fact sheet https://www.hcd.ca.gov/sites/default/files/docs/planning-and-community/aff-hsg-faith-higher-ed-sb-4.pdf

## 2. Families
| Family | Income | % AMI | Band | P(market denial) | Design | P(sustained 10y) | Subsidy PV |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Garcia (4, warehouse + childcare) | $92,000 | 66.4% | very_low | 94% | 4% / 40y / cap 35% / reserve $0 / income-indexed | 98.2% | $152,801 |
| Nguyen (3, nurse aide) | $71,000 | 56.9% | very_low | 94% | 4% / 40y / cap 35% / reserve $0 / income-indexed | 99.1% | $212,896 |
| Okafor (5, rideshare + retail) | $108,000 | 72.2% | low | 92% | 4% / 40y / cap 35% / reserve $0 / income-indexed | 96.8% | $107,014 |

Stress tests (sandbox):
- Garcia (4, warehouse + childcare): stress test → base 98.2% -> stressed 97.4% (job loss x1.5, insurance shock p=15%/yr)
- Nguyen (3, nurse aide): stress test → base 99.1% -> stressed 98.7% (job loss x1.5, insurance shock p=15%/yr)
- Okafor (5, rideshare + retail): stress test → base 96.8% -> stressed 94.6% (job loss x1.5, insurance shock p=15%/yr)

Design logic: payment size and liquidity drive default (Ganong & Noel 2020, https://doi.org/10.1257/aer.20181243); stewardship cures most serious delinquencies (Thaden 2011). Income limits: CA HCD 2026 https://www.hcd.ca.gov/sites/default/files/docs/grants-and-funding/income-limits-2026.pdf

## 3. Capital
Per-home cost $539,062 (hard $431,250, soft $107,812, land $0 via SB 4 ground lease — assumption). Each 0% first mortgage has face value $519,192 but PV $268,655 at 5%. Gap after CalHome + AHP (assumed $100k/home): $162,907 per home → $16,290,679 philanthropy for 100 homes.

Demand (HMDA 2024, real loan data): 1,458 low-income OC purchase applications, 24% denied, 206 for debt-to-income. Source: https://ffiec.cfpb.gov/data-browser/

Funding stack:
- Faith-land ground lease (SB 4): Land contributed or ground-leased by congregation; by-right approval, 45-yr ownership deed restriction (https://www.hcd.ca.gov/sites/default/files/docs/planning-and-community/aff-hsg-faith-higher-ed-sb-4.pdf)
- CalHome (HCD Homeownership Super NOFA): Nonprofits eligible; homeownership development loans and first-time buyer assistance (https://www.hcd.ca.gov/funding/hosn)
- FHLBank San Francisco AHP: Owner-occupied <=80% AMI; via member bank; 2026 General Fund $60.1M (https://www.fhlbsf.com/products/community-programs-grants/ahp)
- Welfare exemption (RTC 214.15 / 214.15.1): Property tax exemption while nonprofit holds homes for sale to low-income buyers; 214.15.1 operative to 2027 lien date (https://www.boe.ca.gov/proptaxes/pdf/lta23044.pdf)
- Keys to 100 philanthropy: 2026 gala raised $330,000 (https://habitatoc.org/keys-to-100-raises-330000-for-affordable-homeownership-in-orange-county/)

Sensitivity (sandbox):
```
hard$/sf  disc   gap/home   total(100)
     325    4%     57,603    5,760,316
     325    5%     91,033    9,103,279
     325    6%    119,141   11,914,126
     375    4%    129,477   12,947,716
     375    5%    162,907   16,290,679
     375    6%    191,015   19,101,526
     425    4%    201,353   20,135,316
     425    5%    234,783   23,478,279
     425    6%    262,891   26,289,126
```

## Model governance
Market-gap model 20261031_154236 (AUC 0.7824), max race-group calibration gap 0.0063; protected attributes excluded from features and promotion is gated on fairness (Fuster et al. 2022, https://doi.org/10.1111/jofi.13090).

## 4. Existing homeowners (HomeKeeper)
Portfolio of 100 homeowners (synthetic families; incomes sampled from 2024 HMDA OC applicants within Habitat OC's 30-80% AMI band). Over 10 years, 87 keep their homes with Keystone designs plus stewardship, against 58 with market-rate loans. The steward made 77 early contacts. At month 36, 1 families need attention. Most urgent:
- **Mai Santos** (90+ days late; Thin cash buffer): Budget coaching; set up an automatic reserve deposit. Draft: "Hi Mai, this is your Habitat steward. We noticed things may be tight this month. We have options that can lower your payment for a while. Can we talk this week?"

Why stewardship: https://www.lincolninst.edu/publications/working-papers/stable-home-ownership-turbulent-economy/

## Next three actions
1. Title-check the shortlisted APNs and open SB 4 conversations with the top congregations.
2. Pre-qualify applicant families with the designs above; enrol all in post-purchase stewardship.
3. Submit CalHome + FHLBank SF AHP applications sized to the per-home gap.

Model inputs not drawn from a cited source are assumptions (see keystone://assumptions).

## Evidence
- Thaden, E. (2011). Stable Home Ownership in a Turbulent Economy. Lincoln Institute WP. https://www.lincolninst.edu/publications/working-paper
